summary: Attempt 1 had left the harness (internal/testutil/program), the stdlib DevTools driver in headless, the ten E-001/E-002 ledger bodies, the E-003 and E-004 line 1 ports, the checker core and the Python snapshots. I kept all of it after checking it. The ten Go bodies and all twelve snapshots hash, in canonical form, to the bodies I read in place from the ledger (epics 39-44, read-only) and to the in-tree Python files. Four things in it were broken and are fixed: the SL-015 fitness rules were folded across lines, so they never loaded; m1's exception was missing; a stray CR made git treat fitness.yaml as binary; default_browser_test.go had no final newline. I wrote the E-004 line 2 tests (deep threads over HTTP, and the toggle plus the 360/400/1000 px look in Chrome), E-005, and both E-006 ports. I also wrote the mapping table (22 sources, 363 rows), whose sites are derived from the snapshots by the checker itself, plus the checker's gap test and a go list -deps check that no acceptance test links the product. The build-tagged breaks test compiles seven trigger overlays, at least one per epic, each with a synchronous 'fired' mark, and every one fails its epic's test. A build-tagged whole-suite check covers C1 and C2. Finally, the closed import/launch spelling corpus and Q-035's EvalSymlinks refusal are in.

TestPortedCheckerRefusesGaps builds a small world and requires a refusal for each of these: a site with no row, a row past the end of the source, an untagged Ported row, a stray tag, a missing function, an Amended or Superseded row with no Why, a Superseded row that names a By, a Verbatim or snapshot sha256 mismatch, a Go body with no Verbatim row, a fake-side row mapped to a reason, a duplicate id or line, an undeclared source, a missing Helper test, a Verbatim Python row, and a tag not on a check. The hand-written count no longer exists (M1). TestPortedAssertionsHaveAGoTest passes on the real 363 rows.

TestBrokenProgramsFailTheirAcceptanceTests (tag sc042breaks) first requires all seven tests to pass as-is. Then, for each overlay break, it requires 'installed' and 'fired' marks and '--- FAIL'. Measured in 55 s: all seven failed for the behaviour, e.g. E001 '/admin answered 200', E002 'its row shows 0 times opened', E003 'got [0 0], want [1 1]', E004 'not shown beneath comment-1', E005 'shows no element id=feedback-<n>', E006 placeholder and block.

TestE004DeepThreadsAndBranchPages runs seedBody on the https base. Levels 1-5 are on the page and level 6 is not, the depths are [1..5], 'continue this thread' is present, levels 7-8 are posted from the branch page and land there, there is a link back, no page is deeper than 5, the site script loads, and the CSP forbids scripts. DeepThread's seed checks run after that.

Completeness holds by construction, built in the critic's version. Sites() finds every site in the committed canonical snapshot: assert, self.assert*/fail, raise, sys/os._exit, a return of a non-zero code, and the call of any def whose body holds a site. Comments and strings are blanked first. Check requires a row at every site line, and rows may add extra sites (L221, L74, L26 and the stand-in refusals). Verbatim Go bodies are exempt, covered by their sha256. The Assertions field is gone.

The builder's first step was the in-place mode=ro SELECT of epics 39-44. Every body's canonical sha256 matches the committed snapshot or Go file, and these are the Editions in rows_test.go. A tag now has to sit on, or just above, the statement that checks (or on the first line of the block that line opens), not anywhere in the function. Two duties are code review's by decision and are not done here: re-running the in-place SELECT, and recording agree or disagree for each Ported row.

Before the change TestRulesHoldOnTheTree failed with 'internal/testutil/program/program.go violates the rule'; now it passes. Corpus row idp-q100 pins it.

Built the critic's version. The import rules (acceptance tests and test helpers) match any import spec of a module package except internal/testutil/: single, grouped, aliased, dot or blank, either quote, with a trailing comment or semicolon, CRLF, at end of file. TestAcceptanceLinksNoneOfTheProduct backs them by construction: it runs go list -deps -test from the GOMOD directory and refuses every package outside std, internal/testutil/ and tests/acceptance/, which includes modernc.org/sqlite and golang.org/x/oauth2. Rule 3 now covers headless/*.go except headless.go and *_test.go, and matches \bos\.(Getenv|LookupEnv|Environ|ExpandEnv)\b. Rule 4 matches the names CHROME_BIN and HBAND_TEST_BROWSER, --/-// flags in either quote style including remote-debugging-pipe, and browser names. The holes are named in each because and pinned quiet. Before the fix, 41 fire rows of the corpus failed against attempt 1's rules (run recorded in tests); after it, all rows pass in Go, and Python's re agrees on all 81 rows of the new rules.

Visitor.Do(t, *http.Request) and Visitor.Request let header names stay in the _test.go callers. visitor.go names no header. E-003's forged() sends Origin, Referer and Sec-Fetch-Site cross-site through Do.

The structural check lives in one helper, internal/testutil/outside.MustBeOutside. Both paths go through Abs and EvalSymlinks, with the nearest existing parent for a folder not yet made, which expands 8.3 short names. The module root comes from `go env GOMOD` through exec, not from an environment read. Build, Start, headless.Open, headless.Shot and the breaks test call it for every folder they make. The repository walk that remains covers only cmd/, internal/ and tests/.

Canonical() strips a BOM, turns CRLF into LF and trims to exactly one trailing newline. Every Edition is sha256(Canonical(text)), in-tree sources included, so no git blob ids remain. Ledger editions were computed in my mode=ro SELECT from each item's JSON-decoded body string, never from a committed file. A new subtest requires a CRLF+BOM checkout of a snapshot to still match its Edition, because core.autocrlf=true here would make one.

deviations: The ported package is test-only: attempt 1's non-test tests/acceptance/ported/ported.go is renamed ported_test.go, the table is in rows_test.go and the checks in check_test.go. The design named ported_test.go, and the stack line says tests/acceptance holds test-only packages.

New package internal/testutil/outside, which is not in the design's component list. It is the single mustBeOutsideModule helper that the m4 critic prescribed, used by both program and headless. headless now imports it.

New build-tagged package tests/acceptance/suite (TestSuiteWithoutABrowser, TestSuiteInChrome). The design's C1/C2 check commands were PowerShell text matches, which M-add-3's decision replaced with -json event parsing; this package gives those cases a command with no shell syntax. Rule 4 excepts tests/acceptance/suite/**, because the package removes CHROME_BIN from, or passes it into, the inner go test; it starts and chooses no browser.

Rule 4 bans the words CHROME_BIN and HBAND_TEST_BROWSER anywhere in tests/acceptance, not only inside Getenv("..."), so os.Environ scans and backquotes are caught. A bare 'chrome' cannot be banned, because the verbatim E-001/E-002 bodies use it for their User-Agent; this is a named hole.

The tag-placement rule accepts a tag on the line of, or the line just above, a checking statement, or on the first line of the block that the line below opens (an if, for or case). The critic's text said only 'same line or line just above'; without the extra allowance, a check written as `if cond { t.Fatalf }` could not be tagged.

The def-call propagation the critic prescribed for Sites flags name collisions as sites: in the E-004 line 2 body, built-in open() and read() share names with Chrome.open/Chrome.read, at L58, L118, L181, L207, L208, L318 and L319. Each such line has a row saying so. Those inside the stand-in GitHub are Helper rows to fakegithub; the others are Superseded 'not an assertion', or Ported to headless.Open where they are the DevToolsActivePort read.

seedBody (the E-004 line 2 body's posting and HTTP checks) runs in both E-004 line 2 tests. The browser test therefore re-makes the HTTP checks on loopback http before its Chrome checks. The production-shaped https run is TestE004DeepThreadsAndBranchPages.

The Go Visitor does not imitate the Python Browser's extras: a Chrome User-Agent, X-Forwarded-For 192.0.2.10, CSRF hidden fields and Origin on every post. hband has no CSRF tokens, CrossOriginProtection accepts requests with no Origin or Sec-Fetch-Site, and no E-003..E-006 assertion depends on User-Agent or forwarded address. Anonymous and blocked-account posts use Post without following, where the Python followed hband's redirects up to the stand-in; those sites assert only status < 500.
